q: The natural extension of a non-invertible measure-preserving system (X,μ,T) is the invertible system (X̃,μ̃,T̃) where X̃ is:
opts: The inverse limit: {(x₀,x₁,...) : T(xₙ₊₁) = xₙ for all n}
The suspension of X over T
exp: The natural extension X̃ = {(xₙ)_{n≤0} : T(xₙ) = xₙ₊₁} is the 'smallest' invertible extension. T̃ is the left-shift. The natural extension of the Gauss map is the two-sided continued fraction map, central in the metric theory of continued fractions.
